title.narrative: Supporting socio-economic reinsertion of 405 vulnerable youth and children in Masisi and Goma, DRC

description.narrative: The Democratic Republic of Congo in general, and in particular North Kivu province, has faced an armed conflict whose harmful effects have deeply affected children. Children experienced serious violations of their rights, including their recruitment into armed forces and militia groups, abductions, massacres, and family separation. According to the 2012 Humanitarian action plan from OCHA DRC, more than 40,000 children are non accompanied and vulnerable; 2000 child soldiers removed from armed forces; 1.7 million 3-17 year olds are not at school. During our field monitoring visit and workshops with partners, we decided to contribute to restore hope and dignity in the life of Congolese children and young people with a sustainable protection and early recovery Programme. CAJED is one of our long lasting partners based in North Kivu, working in this area of child protection, with over 15 years of experience with CAFOD. This project presented by CAJED will be implemented in Goma town and Masisi. CAJED will focus on three main activities to bring lasting change to the life of 405 children and young people: • Formal Education reinsertion: Community members and schools responsible will work together with social workers to identify, sensitize vulnerable out of school children to attend school in the next school year; • Vocational training and life skills: Some vulnerable children who will not able to attend formal education, will be assessed, and trained in vocational trainings, and life skills. At the end of each six month training cycles; trainees will be equipped to hold their own workshops with closed supervision and support from CAJED; • Small scale trading: There are some youth who will not like to attend school or vocational trainings. They will be trained in small scale trading, mainly in groups of 4 to 7 members. A strong market analysis will be conducted by the partner prior to cash transfer. • Special focus will be given to Girls, CAJED will work in consortium with a female led organisation named APROFIM, specialising in Girls Education and support. • In the meantime, some schools and training centres will be rehabilitated and equipped. The overall outcome for this programme is to improve the socio-economic life of children and young people so that they will no longer be interested to return to armed groups and militias. This will contribute surely to peace building and stability in the targeted area.
